Hua Zheng

Sr. Research Scientist · Meta

Sunnyvale, California

I am a Sr. Research Scientist at Meta, where I work on the Generative Ads Recommendation Model (GEM) and memory scaling for large-scale recommendation systems. My research focuses on developing new knowledge transfer techniques and transfer learning paradigms that distill the capabilities of large foundation models into the compact, efficient models that power real-time production systems — preserving as much of a foundation model's predictive quality as possible while meeting the strict latency, cost, and reliability constraints of serving billions of requests. My broader interests span deep reinforcement learning, foundation models, and knowledge distillation, informed by hands-on experience with large-scale data engineering, search, and recommender systems.

LoopFM: Learning frOm HistOrical RePresentations of Foundation Model for Recommendation

Hua Zheng, Shali Jiang, Boyang Liu, Laming Chen, Kenny Lov, Chuanqi Xu, Lisang Ding, Qinghai Zhou, Can Cui, Xiaolong Liu, Xiaoyi Liu, Yasmine Badr, Xin Xu, Mingfu Liang, Jiyan Yang, Ellie Dingqiao Wen, Gerard Jonathan Mugisha Akkerhuis, Jason Rudy, Xi Liu, Chenxiao Guan, Rong Jin, Ruichao Qiu, Xian Chen, Zhehui Zhou, Ping Chen, Rui Yang, Haicheng Chen, Meet Raval, Song Zhou, Dharak Kharod, Shuyu Xu, Xingyuan Wang, Liang Tao, Qiang Jin, Qiao Yang, Wankun Zhu, Qin Huang, Yuzhen Huang, Darren Liu, Parish Aggarwal, Hui Zhou, Erzhuo Wang, Shuo Chang, Xiaorui Gan, Wenlin Chen, Santanu Kolay, Huayu Li

arXiv preprint arXiv:2605.29280 · 2026

Knowledge distillation passes only a single scalar prediction from a foundation model (FM) to compact vertical models (VMs), so the transfer ratio shrinks as FMs grow. LoopFM opens a high-bandwidth channel instead: FM intermediate embeddings, structured as input features (e.g. user history sequences), feed downstream VMs — with no real-time FM inference at serving and no architectural coupling.

Figure 1 from the paper — LoopFM overview: historical FM embeddings as structured VM input features, with internal production and public-benchmark results.
≈2× knowledge transfer ratio over KD · +1.22% conversion (industrial launches)
Abstract

Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers a single scalar prediction from a large foundation model (FM) to compact vertical models (VMs), suffering from diminishing transfer ratio as a single scalar cannot convey the rich intermediate knowledge that larger FMs learn. LoopFM structures FM intermediate embeddings as input features for downstream VMs, without requiring real-time FM inference at serving and architectural coupling between FM and VM. A theoretical framework gives a gain decomposition and transfer-ratio analysis. On three public benchmarks LoopFM shows strong AUC improvements (6%+ on TaobaoAd); on industrial-scale systems (billions of examples, trillion-parameter FMs) it approximately doubles the knowledge transfer ratio on top of KD, delivering +0.5% conversion improvement in the first half after launch, and +1.03% / +1.22% from two launches in the subsequent half.

Generalizable Multi-Pass Training of Ads Recommendation Models with Foundation Model Guidance

Yunzhe Qi, Qinghai Zhou, Boyang Liu, Can Cui, Hua Zheng, Qiuling Suo, Mingfu Liang, Kenny Lov, Xi Liu, Shali Jiang, Laming Chen, Wen-Yen Chen, Rong Jin, Shuo Chang, Jingrui He, Huayu Li

Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD 2026) · pp. 4000–4011

High-capacity CTR models for ads recommendation suffer one-epoch overfitting: performance peaks after a single pass over the data, and further epochs memorize noisy click data and degrade generalization. TeMPO fixes this with guidance from a recommendation foundation model — the serving model learns not only from click labels but from the richer patterns the FM captures — so multi-pass training keeps improving instead of overfitting. Backed by theoretical analysis and experiments on public datasets and Meta's large-scale advertising system.

Figure 1 from the paper — multi-pass training compared: standard one-pass, a naive second pass that overfits noisy clicks, and TeMPO's teacher-guided second pass.
TeMPO · multi-pass training that improves instead of overfitting · KDD 2026

Variance Reduction Based Experience Replay for Policy Optimization

Hua Zheng, Wei Xie, M. Ben Feng, Keilung Choy

arXiv preprint arXiv:2602.05379 · 2026 (journal version in revision at IISE Transactions)

Classical experience replay reuses all past samples uniformly, ignoring that they differ in value. VRER selectively reuses the most relevant historical trajectories to cut the variance of policy-gradient estimates; the resulting PG-VRER algorithm comes with finite-time convergence guarantees and an explicit bias–variance trade-off for reusing older experience. Ships with the open-source vrer-pg library (PPO / TRPO / VPG).

From the paper — learning curves (mean ± 95% CI): VPG / PPO / TRPO with and without VRER
Finite-time convergence guarantees · bias–variance trade-off characterized
Abstract

Effective RL for complex stochastic systems requires leveraging historical data from previous iterations. Classical experience replay treats all past observations uniformly. VRER selectively reuses informative samples to reduce variance in policy gradient estimation; it is algorithm-agnostic and forms the basis of the sample-efficient off-policy algorithm PG-VRER. A novel analysis framework explicitly captures dependencies from Markovian dynamics and behavior-policy interactions, yielding finite-time convergence guarantees and a fundamental bias–variance trade-off: reusing older experience increases bias but reduces gradient variance. Empirically, VRER consistently accelerates policy learning over state-of-the-art policy optimization algorithms.

Digital Twin Calibration with Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

Hua Zheng, Wei Xie, Ilya O. Ryzhov, Keilung Choy

arXiv preprint arXiv:2501.02205 · 2025

The Actor–Simulator framework folds digital-twin calibration into model-based RL: the twin is calibrated and the control policy is optimized jointly, with policy performance guiding data collection — provably converging to the optimal policy and beating methods that assume the model is right.

Figure 1 from the paper — schematic of iPSC culture in a bioreactor and the intracellular metabolic network.
Provable convergence to the optimal policy
Abstract

Traditional model-based control relies on restrictive structural assumptions and ignores parameter uncertainty — critical in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, where dynamics are complex, not fully known, and data is limited. The Actor–Simulator jointly calibrates the digital twin and searches for an optimal control policy, accounting for and reducing model error, balancing exploration and exploitation by using policy performance to guide data collection. The approach provably converges to the optimal policy and outperforms existing methods in extensive numerical experiments in the biopharmaceutical manufacturing domain.

SiGeo: Sub-One-Shot NAS via Information Theory and Geometry of Loss Landscape

Hua Zheng, Kuang-Hung Liu, Igor Fedorov, Xin Zhang, Wen-Yen Chen, Wei Wen

Proceedings of the 30th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD 2024)

One-shot NAS is accurate but expensive; zero-shot proxies are cheap but unreliable, especially for recommender systems. SiGeo bridges them with a sub-one-shot paradigm: warm the supernet up on a small data subset, then score architectures with a proxy grounded in information theory and the geometry of the loss landscape.

Figure 1 from the paper — SiGeo-NAS under one-shot, sub-one-shot, and zero-shot settings, and the loss-landscape geometry behind the proxy.
≈60% lower compute than one-shot NAS at comparable quality · KDD 2024
Abstract

Neural Architecture Search (NAS) automates neural network design. One-shot NAS reduces cost by weight sharing but still requires extensive training; zero-shot NAS uses training-free proxies but cannot use information gained as a network improves and is unreliable in complex domains like RecSys. We introduce a sub-one-shot paradigm bridging the two: the supernet is trained on only a small subset of the training data (warm-up). Within this framework, SiGeo is a proxy founded on a novel theoretical framework connecting supernet warm-up with proxy efficacy. SiGeo consistently outperforms state-of-the-art NAS proxies on established benchmarks, and with warm-up achieves performance comparable to weight-sharing one-shot NAS at ~60% lower computational cost.

Stochastic Biological System-of-Systems Modelling for iPSC Culture

Hua Zheng, Sarah W. Harcum, Jinxiang Pei, Wei Xie

Communications Biology · 2024

iPSC aggregates starve their own cores of nutrients. The Bio-SoS framework models cell-to-cell interactions across cell, aggregate, and population levels — stochastic metabolic networks, aggregation kinetics, and reaction–diffusion — with a variance decomposition that quantifies how factors like aggregate size drive product heterogeneity.

Figure 1 from the paper — the Bio-SoS framework: population balance, reaction–diffusion, and stochastic single-cell models.
Identifies aggregate size as a key driver of product heterogeneity
Abstract

Large-scale iPSC manufacturing is essential for cell therapies, yet aggregates in suspension bioreactors create nutrient-poor, waste-rich cores and heterogeneous cell populations. The Biological System-of-Systems (Bio-SoS) framework models cell-to-cell interactions, spatial and metabolic heterogeneity, and micro-environment response using stochastic metabolic reaction networks, aggregation kinetics, and reaction–diffusion mechanisms, characterizing causal interdependencies at individual-cell, aggregate, and population levels. Its modular design integrates data across monolayer and aggregate processes, and a variance decomposition analysis quantifies the impact of factors such as aggregate size on cell product health and quality heterogeneity.

Policy Optimization in Bayesian Network Hybrid Models of Biomanufacturing Processes

Hua Zheng, Wei Xie, Ilya O. Ryzhov, Dongming Xie

INFORMS Journal on Computing · 2022

A model-based RL framework that reaches human-level control in low-data environments: a dynamic Bayesian network captures the causal interdependencies of the bioprocess, and a provably convergent stochastic gradient method optimizes control policies that are robust to model risk.

Figure 1 from the paper — network model of an integrated biopharmaceutical production process, with (sₜ, aₜ) as CQAs/CPPs at each time period.
Human-level control in low-data regimes · INFORMS J. on Computing 2022
Abstract

Biomanufacturing processes require close monitoring and control amid complex dynamics with many interdependent factors and extremely limited data. We develop a model-based RL framework achieving human-level control in low-data environments. A dynamic Bayesian network captures causal interdependencies between factors and predicts how input effects propagate through the bioprocess pathways. The model is interpretable and enables policies robust against model risk. We present a computationally efficient, provably convergent stochastic gradient method for optimizing such policies, validated on a realistic application with a multidimensional continuous state.

Personalized Multimorbidity Management for Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Using Reinforcement Learning of Electronic Health Records

Hua Zheng, Ilya O. Ryzhov, Wei Xie, Judy Zhong

Drugs · 2021

An RL prescription policy trained on EHRs of 16,665 type-2-diabetes patients at NYU Langone, jointly optimizing glycemia, blood pressure, and cardiovascular risk. Its recommendations agree with clinicians in 83–98% of encounters — and where they differ, patients' outcomes are significantly better controlled.

Figure 1 (panel A) from the paper — heatmap of where the RL glycemia policy's prescriptions differ from clinicians'.
Fewer uncontrolled A1c / BP / CVD-risk encounters wherever RL differs from clinicians
Abstract

Comorbid chronic conditions are common in type 2 diabetes. We modeled glycemia, blood pressure, and CVD risk using a retrospective cohort of 16,665 T2D patients (NYU Langone, 2009–2017) and trained RL algorithms recommending treatment regimens that optimize cumulative health outcomes from each patient's characteristics and history. Single-outcome RL policies matched clinician prescriptions in 86.1% (glycemia), 82.9% (blood pressure), and 98.4% (CVD) of encounters. Where RL differed, uncontrolled glycemia (35% vs 43%), uncontrolled hypertension (16% vs 27%), and high CVD risk (25% vs 31%) were all significantly less frequent (all p ≤ 0.001).

A Modular Mechanistic In Silico Model for In Vitro Transcription Process Yield and Product Quality Prediction

Keqi Wang, Keilung Choy, Eli Reiser, Jinxiang Pei, Hua Zheng, Aparajita Dasgupta, Fuqiang Cheng, Guogang Dong, Bhanu Chandra Mulukutla, Joshua Mannheimer, Carolyn Huang, Hooman Farsani, Wei Xie

Biotechnology and Bioengineering · 2026

The IVT reaction network behind mRNA manufacturing, decomposed into six kinetic modules — initiation/capping, elongation/truncation, termination/read-through, mRNA degradation, Mg₂PPi precipitation, and pyrophosphate degradation — then reassembled into one predictive model, refined with residual/Shapley sensitivity analysis and Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization.

Figure 2 from the paper — the hybrid (mechanistic + machine learning) workflow for data-informed, mechanism-driven model development and refinement.
Hybrid mechanistic + ML platform for mRNA process design
Abstract

In vitro transcription (IVT) is critical to manufacturing mRNA vaccines and therapeutics; optimizing yield and product quality (capping efficiency, integrity) is mechanistically complex. This modular mechanistic model decomposes the IVT reaction network into six interconnected modules with kinetic models accounting for mass balances, molecular complexation, and enzyme activity, assembled to capture coupled IVT dynamics. Multivariate residual analysis and Shapley-value sensitivity analysis iteratively improve model fidelity, and Gaussian-process batch Bayesian optimization supports efficient parameter estimation — a scalable hybrid (mechanistic + ML) platform for rational design and optimization of mRNA manufacturing.

Some Gaps Between Reinforcement Learning Practice and Theory

May 2022 · Blog · 5 min read

Three places where RL practice quietly departs from the assumptions its theory needs: experience replay makes stored transitions dependent on the current policy, violating conditional unbiasedness; the critic-compatibility conditions behind the policy gradient theorem are rarely satisfied by deep actor–critics; and the discounted objective samples states from the stationary distribution while the theorem is stated under the discounted occupancy.
